key_insight: Boundary slip properties organise a non-self-propelling 2D model microswimmer into trapped, gliding or oscillatory motion, with a universal transition at viscosity ratio σ = 1/2.
engineering_relevance: Tuning fluid viscosity contrasts or wall slip could help control microswimmer trapping and transport near microfluidic boundaries.
method: Represent the microswimmer using a two-dimensional point-singularity model.
Use complex-variable methods to derive explicit motion equations near a flat viscosity interface and a Navier-slip wall.
Analyse dynamical regimes as viscosity ratio or relative slip length varies.
evidence_signal: Analytical results identify three viscosity-controlled regimes and a periodic hydrodynamic bound state with zero net displacement; the abstract reports no experimental validation.
watch_item: The idealised swimmer does not self-propel in unbounded fluid, and its two-dimensional dynamics require validation before application to real three-dimensional swimmers.
paper_title: Dynamics of a two-dimensional microswimmer near a slippery boundary
